newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end softer, but set intra-day high.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end softer, but set intra-day high.

text.p: Toronto stocks finished softer on Thursday as weak gold prices and profit-taking investors ended a two-day rally, analysts said.
The TSE 300 Composite Index slipped 8.0 points to 5380.01 in turnover of 97 million shares worth C$1.4 billion ($1.02 billion).
Declining stocks outnumbered advances 452 to 444 with 311 issues unchanged. But the key index struggled to an intra-day high of 5388.20 before finishing weaker.
"It's still a good looking market. If it wasn't for the golds, Toronto would be up a little bit," said Rolie Bradley, an institutional salesman with Maison Placements Canada Inc.
The precious metals group surrendered 169 points as COMEX gold futures turned lower after a two-day bounce.
COMEX December gold fell US$0.90 to US$381.40 an ounce.
Toronto also suffered modest profit-taking in financial services, conglomerates, base metals and technology. The TSE posted losses in eight of 14 sub-groups.
Gains were led by energy, transport and utility stocks.
Bradley said the market's underlying tone remains firm in the wake of Wednesday's interest rate cuts by the Bank of Canada and the country's major banks.
* Gandalf Technologies Inc. closed down 1.20 to 6.10.
The stock sank to a 52-week low of 5.30 after Gandalf warned investors to expect a net loss for the second quarter.

* Oil stocks received a boost from strong commodity prices. Anderson Exploration Ltd. improved 0.35 to 14.25 on 1.7 million shares, while Poco Petroleums Ltd. gained 0.15 to 11.50 on 1.5 million shares.
* BCE Inc. jumped 0.45 to finish at 59.80 after earlier hitting a 52-week high of 60. The telecommunications giant said today it plans to redeem C$150 million ($110 million) in debentures.
* Laidlaw Inc. class B topped the most-active list, adding 0.10 to 15 on 3.7 million shares.
